rules: Each idea is scored with liquid stand-ins (its 'legs'), so an options or futures idea is scored on the direction of its underlying, not the exact P&L of the structure.
Entry is the first daily close after the idea was published (before 19:00 UTC counts for that day's close; later ideas enter at the next day's close).
Pair return = long-leg return minus short-leg return, weighted by the legs' stated sizes.
Exit is the first of: target hit, stop hit, or horizon expired, checked on daily closes.
Ideas repeated while still open count once. Ideas dropped from the read still run to their exit.

Ideas published before 2026-11-10 had their stand-ins written afterwards from the prose and are marked 'reconstructed'. Their target is the % move the prose stated (low end of a range), their stop is the same size in the other direction, and ideas with no stated % exit at the horizon.
Headline numbers count every idea marked to market (open ones at today's price). Closed-only numbers are biased early on, because ideas that hit targets close sooner than ones that expire.

ideas.name: Long IEF vs short LQD — high grade is widening into the rally
ideas.line: Long IEF / short LQD: IG and BBB spreads widening at z=1.6+
ideas.expr: Equal dollars long IEF against short LQD; both legs liquid, the pair isolates investment-grade spread from duration. Roll monthly.
ideas.thesis: LQD's +2.2% month is entirely duration — IG OAS went from 0.82 to 0.93 and BBB from 1.02 to 1.16 in the same window. Owning Treasuries against corporates captures the one deterioration that has not reversed on any up day.

ideas.name: Short SMH vs long XLV — rent the squeeze, don't marry it
ideas.line: Short SMH / long XLV: semis squeezed, leadership still broken
ideas.expr: Dollar-neutral: short SMH against long XLV. Express the short as SMH puts if you want defined risk through earnings.
ideas.thesis: The squeeze lifted the most damaged names on no new information while the index's biggest stock fell. Healthcare is the opposite: trend up, relative strength up, extended for the right reasons.

ideas.name: Short ETH — the liquidity beta never showed up
ideas.line: Short ETH: no bid in a three-day global squeeze
ideas.expr: Short ETH spot or perp; the cleaner cross is short ETH against long BTC (ETH/BTC -7.1% on the month, 23rd percentile). Size small, this is high-vol.
ideas.thesis: When Korea rips 4.4% and European indices print highs and the most liquidity-sensitive asset in the world goes down, there is no marginal dollar. Reserves -2.1% over three months and RRP at $0.25bn say the same thing.

ideas.name: Long SPLV vs short SPHB — beta is still being de-rated
ideas.line: Long SPLV / short SPHB: high-beta down 18.6% vs low-vol in 1m
ideas.expr: Equal dollars long SPLV against short SPHB. Add a 1-2% notional SPY Dec put spread while VIX/VIX3M is back at 0.9554 and protection is cheap.
ideas.thesis: The regime shift from high beta to quality cash flows has run for a month with acceleration behind it; a one-day +4.2% pop in the ratio is a rental inside a downtrend, and it happened while BBB spreads widened.

ideas.name: Fade the semiconductor squeeze
ideas.line: Short SMH into +7.5% SOXX day as NVDA falls 4.3%
ideas.expr: December SMH 470/430 put spreads, or short SMH against a 1x long SPY leg to isolate the relative call.
ideas.thesis: A one-day +7.5% in SOXX off a month at z=-2.36 is mechanical short covering, and the leader is not confirming it: NVDA -4.3% today, -22.1% on the month, 19th percentile, 12.6% below its 200-day. AVGO is in the 15th percentile, MU -28.7% on the month, SMH/SPY z=-2.7 and rolling over at the 37th percentile. Money is leaving this complex for breadth (RSP/SPY z=3.59) and value (growth/value at the 7th percentile).

ideas.name: Breadth over the index leaders
ideas.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ: RSP/SPY z=3.6, QQQ/SPY 18th pctile
ideas.expr: Long RSP, short QQQ, equal dollars; roll monthly.
ideas.thesis: The leadership transfer is a regime, not a week. Equal weight is +3.7% on the month while the S&P is -3.3%; RSP/SPY z=3.59 with acceleration 3.28. QQQ/SPY is -6.5% on the month at z=-2.57, rolling over, 18th percentile. Growth/value z=-3.08 at the 7th percentile, MTUM z=-3.01, high-beta/low-vol -18.6% on the month. Beneath it, the new leaders are real businesses re-rating: HD +21.6%, MCD +19.6%, LLY +19.7%, XLV z=2.40, financials relative strength +9.6%.

ideas.name: Energy equities mark to $92 Brent
ideas.line: Short XLE/XOP: energy hasn't marked to $92 Brent
ideas.expr: Short XLE outright, or buy Jan XLE 58 puts; higher-beta version is short XOP against long XOM to keep the integrated hedge.
ideas.thesis: Brent has fallen 12.4% in a month and gasoline 20.0%, yet the only sector that worked all year is down 2.7% on the month and still 5.4% above its 200-day. Earnings revisions follow the strip, not the tape, and the group is the single most crowded long left in US equities.

ideas.name: Fade the AI-power squeeze
ideas.line: Fade the AI-power squeeze: short VST, GEV, NLR
ideas.expr: Short VST and GEV outright, NLR as the basket leg, roughly a third each; use Jan VST puts if borrow is expensive.
ideas.thesis: The power/nuclear/grid complex is the purest leveraged bet on AI capex and it is being de-rated, not corrected. A one-day 10% move in a stock that is 18% below its 200-day and in the 16th percentile of its year is short covering, and it hands you the re-entry.

ideas.name: Long India vs short broad EM
ideas.line: Long INDA vs short EEM: the only EM with a tailwind FX
ideas.expr: Long INDA, short an equal dollar amount of EEM. Size 1:1; roll monthly.
ideas.thesis: EEM/SPY at z=-1.64 is a blended average hiding a 35-point internal gap. India has a falling USD/INR, accelerating local equities and no semiconductor concentration; EEM is one-third Korea/Taiwan semis plus a Brazil accident.

ideas.name: Long India / short Brazil
ideas.line: Long INDA vs short EWZ — EM dispersion, 35pts and widening
ideas.expr: Buy INDA, short EWZ, dollar-neutral notional. Overlay: short USDBRL vol or own 3m USDBRL calls as the hedge leg if you cannot short EWZ.
ideas.thesis: EM is not one asset. India has a falling dollar cross (USDINR -2.6% on the month, z=-2.55) funding a 10.4% monthly equity gain; Brazil has a 3-sigma currency blowout funding a 24.5% monthly equity collapse. These are the two tails of the same EEM index that screens as merely 'weak' at z=-1.64.

ideas.name: Short AUD/USD
ideas.line: Short AUDUSD — dollar squeeze plus copper rolling over
ideas.expr: Short spot AUDUSD at 0.6868, or buy 2-month 0.6700 AUD puts. Equity-sleeve alternative: short FXA.
ideas.thesis: The second leg of this correction is a funding event, not an equity event. DXY at the 95th percentile with EURUSD at the 1.5th and AUD as the highest-beta G10 proxy to both Chinese metals demand and global risk appetite. Copper -5.1% on the month and COPX -14.8% remove the terms-of-trade support.

ideas.name: Short the crowded defensive
ideas.line: Short MCD — z=3.84, acceleration 3.98, already rolling over
ideas.expr: Short MCD outright at 276.52, or buy Jan 270/245 put spreads. Pair version: short MCD vs long XLV if you want sector-neutral.
ideas.thesis: MCD is the most statistically extended name in the dataset: +19.8% on the month at z=3.84 with acceleration z=3.98, and the trend state has already flipped to rolling_over. It is a crowded flight-to-safety trade in a stock with negative 1-year performance (-5.0%) and relative strength vs the S&P already marked 'down'. The defensive bid cracked today.

ideas.name: India over Korea
ideas.line: Long INDA vs short EWY: the EM index is two markets now
ideas.expr: Long INDA, short EWY, equal notional. Size for 2x the vol of EWY.
ideas.thesis: EM is not one trade. India is a crude importer with a strengthening currency going into a cheaper-oil world; Korea is a levered semis export proxy mid-liquidation with its currency breaking.

ideas.name: Fuel winners vs oil services
ideas.line: Long JETS / short OIH as the Iran premium drains
ideas.expr: Long JETS, short OIH, 1:1 notional (OIH carries more beta, so trim to 0.8x short).
ideas.thesis: A peace-driven unwind of an eight-month war premium transfers margin from producers and service providers to fuel consumers. Services have the worst structure in the energy complex; airlines have the best operating leverage to a 17% weekly fuel move.

ideas.name: Energy equity catches up to $99 Brent
ideas.line: Long XOP — crude +5% while E&Ps sold off 2.9%
ideas.expr: Long XOP 60% / XLE 40%, hedged with a half-weight SPY short to strip index beta out of a high-vol tape.
ideas.thesis: Yesterday energy equity capitulated to crude on an up day for oil; today crude ripped again and the equity still fell. Brent is 99.32 (+63.2% YTD, 6.9% above its 200-day) and WTI 91.26, yet XOP is only 2.3% above its 200-day and XOM/CVX are up just 0.5% and 2.6% on the month. Energy is one of three sectors with positive 3-month relative strength (XLE rs +11.5%) and it is the natural beneficiary if the new Washington balance slows permitting for everything except what is already producing.

ideas.name: Fade the VIX term-structure panic
ideas.line: Short Dec VIX vs long Mar; or sell 1m SPX put spreads
ideas.expr: Short December VIX futures against long March VIX futures (calendar), or sell SPX 1-month 8-12% OTM put spreads. Small size — this is the one trade in the book that is short the tape.
ideas.thesis: VIX/VIX3M at 1.1029 is the 100th percentile of the year and a 24.8% one-day jump. Backwardation that deep without a credit event has historically been a two-to-four week mean-reverter, and the hedges are already bought: SKEW fell 1.0% to 149.37 today, so tail demand did not expand — only spot vol did. Pair this with the HYG short above and you are long the real risk and short the panic premium.

ideas.name: Housing gets the cuts before chips do
ideas.line: Long ITB — rate relief lands on homebuilders first
ideas.expr: Long ITB, or DHI outright; finance it by shorting XLI, which is -11.8% over three months with relative strength down.
ideas.thesis: The only cyclical group with improving absolute and relative trend is housing. ITB is +13.4% on the month and turning up, XHB/SPY is z=2.47, DHI closed green today and is +15.3% on the month, and HD is +22.1% on the month at z=3.07. The 5y yield is -44bp on the month and the 30y mortgage has finally started to follow, -10bp to 7.18. If the front end is right about cuts, this is where the earnings revisions happen, and it has zero AI-capex exposure.

ideas.name: Short the AI power/electrification complex
ideas.line: Short VST/GEV/ETN basket: AI capex derivative is breaking
ideas.expr: Equal-weight short VST, GEV, ETN, CEG (25% each); or buy Jan put spreads 10-15% OTM in VST and GEV. Hedge 30% of notional with long XLU to isolate the AI-capex component.
ideas.thesis: The chips cracked first; the downstream monetizers of AI capex are now repricing with a lag and from far higher relative valuations. These are crowded 2025-26 momentum vehicles with no index-level support, and the rotation out of AI is feeding them to the bid in consumer and healthcare.

ideas.name: Long Germany/UK vs short Korea
ideas.line: Long EWG+EWU / short EWY: capex beta vs domestic earnings
ideas.expr: Long 50% EWG + 50% EWU vs short EWY, equal notional, FX unhedged.
ideas.thesis: Korea is the purest listed proxy for AI memory capex and is unwinding with circuit breakers; Germany and the UK are domestic-earnings markets making 52-week highs with falling global yields and a soft dollar. The pair is long the rotation's destination and short its source.

ideas.name: Long gold miners vs the metal
ideas.line: Long GDX / short GLD: the equity discount is finally closing
ideas.expr: Long GDX (add 25% GDXJ and a GDX Jan 90 call overlay) vs short GLD at ~0.6x notional to neutralize bullion beta.
ideas.thesis: Miners spent the entire gold drawdown trading worse than the metal; that discount is now unwinding with the metal stabilizing. Operating leverage works in both directions and the ratio has barely started.

ideas.name: Short energy equities vs long S&P
ideas.line: Short XLE/XOP vs long SPY — crude -11% on the week, XLE +14% over 200d
ideas.expr: Short XLE and XOP in equal notional (60/40) against a long SPY leg of the same gross. Or buy XLE Jan puts at the money.
