ideas.name: Long sterling against the dollar
ideas.line: Long GBPUSD 1.3501 — best momentum in G10, DXY accelerating lower
ideas.expr: Long GBPUSD spot or Dec futures. Fund partly by shorting USDCAD if you want a pure dollar-short expression rather than a cable call.
ideas.thesis: Sterling is the only G10 currency with a clean turn: +2.0% on the month, z=0.89, trend turning up with acceleration 1.36, 0.5% above its 200-day at the 60th percentile. The euro is still structurally offered (16th percentile, down trend), so cable is the cleaner long dollar-short.

ideas.name: Long Europe, short Japan
ideas.line: Long EWG/EWU vs short EWJ — DAX 92nd pctile, Nikkei z=-2.38
ideas.expr: Long EWG and EWU (50/50) versus short EWJ, dollar-neutral notional. Futures alternative: long DAX, short Nikkei 225, FX-hedged.
ideas.thesis: Europe is the only developed region where price, breadth and relative strength all point the same direction, while Japan has lost the one thing that was carrying it — a weak yen is no longer generating index gains, which means the semis/export complex inside the Nikkei is doing the damage.

ideas.name: Mean-revert the dispersion extreme
ideas.line: Long QQQ vs short RSP — QQQ/SPY z=-2.72 vs RSP/SPY z=+3.34
ideas.expr: Long QQQ against short RSP, equal dollar notional. Cheaper convex version: QQQ Dec call spreads financed by selling RSP upside, now that VIX is 18.39.
ideas.thesis: Every dispersion gauge in the book is pinned at a multi-year extreme and the vol that caused it has just collapsed. RSP/SPY at z=+3.34 with acceleration +3.76 is the most stretched single reading in the digest; QQQ/SPY at z=-2.72 with acceleration -3.21 is the mirror. These do not persist past the volatility event that creates them.

ideas.name: Long USD/BRL
ideas.line: Long USDBRL 5.4623 — BRL can't rally on a 0.6% dollar drop
ideas.expr: Long USDBRL via 3-month NDF or BRL futures. Equity expression for those who can't trade FX: short EWZ.
ideas.thesis: Brazil is a standalone stress, and the cleanest tell is that the real weakened on a day the dollar broke. Local equity is confirming: BVSP -13.8% on the month at z=-2.80, EWZ -16.9% and 14.3% below its 200-day at the 14th percentile.

ideas.name: Long XLY vs short XLP
ideas.line: Long XLY / short XLP: fade the 2.7-sigma staples melt-up
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XLY, short XLP. Size 1.5% of NAV per leg.
ideas.thesis: Staples are the most overbought defensive on the board after a +10.5% month at z=2.72 with acceleration 2.79, sitting at the 89th percentile — a bond proxy bought for the wrong reason. With yields turning back up, the duration support disappears. Discretionary is the mirror: XLY/XLP sits at just the 11.6th percentile of its 52-week range.

ideas.name: Long GRID / electrification basket
ideas.line: Long GRID: power chain bottoming as semis stop bleeding
ideas.expr: Long GRID at 167.40, or an equal-weight basket of ETN, GEV, VST, CEG.
ideas.thesis: The AI-power complex was liquidated with the semis — GRID -8.5% on the month at z=-1.64 and 6.0% below its 200-day, NLR -12.4% at the 0.5 percentile, VST at the 9th percentile. If the semi liquidation is ending, the second-derivative trade is the electrical chain, which carries real order books, not multiple.

ideas.name: Long ITB — duration rally in equity form
ideas.line: Long ITB: +4.6% today, +11.9% on month, 10y -37bp on the month
ideas.expr: Long ITB (or XHB for broader supply-chain beta); express leveraged via Jan ITB 100/115 call spreads. Pair hedge: short a half-weight of XLU, which is rolling over at z=1.86 after a 9.6% monthly run.
ideas.thesis: The 37bp monthly drop in the 10-year is finally reaching the most rate-sensitive equity cohort, and housing has the rare combination of improving relative strength and a depressed starting point — XHB/SPY is still at the 32nd percentile of its 52-week range, so this is early, not chased.

ideas.name: Long XLF / short XLK
ideas.line: Long XLF vs short XLK: leadership handoff, +10.1% vs -10.8% RS
ideas.expr: Dollar-neutral: long XLF, short XLK. Add KRE as a third of the long leg for the steepener optionality.
ideas.thesis: Tech is losing leadership while financials gain it, and the financial complex is broad — banks, regionals, insurance and brokers all turned up together. XLK's relative strength is rolling over from an extreme; XLF's is turning up from a base at the 93rd percentile of price.

ideas.name: Energy equity, the only up-tape
ideas.line: Long XOP/XLE — green on a -1.8% SPX day, 100th pctile
ideas.expr: Core long XLE, higher-beta sleeve in XOP; add XOM and CVX as the quality anchors. Fund by trimming materials/XME.
ideas.thesis: Crude at 102.95 is +13.9% on the month and +79.3% YTD, and energy equities are the one group with positive absolute, relative and acceleration scores. Oil/gold at a 52-week high says the cash flow is real, not a hedge bid.

ideas.name: Gold over silver into the liquidation
ideas.line: Long GLD vs short SLV — gold/silver z=2.02, +13.5% 1m
ideas.expr: Long GLD, short an equal-notional silver position (SLV or COMEX silver); keep gold leg slightly larger to carry the de-grossing beta.
ideas.thesis: This is a margin-driven unwind of crowded precious metals longs, and the industrial/levered leg always goes first. Silver is -18.2% on the month at z=-2.03 and platinum -15.7%; gold is -7.2%. The ratio is the cleanest way to own the liquidation without calling the bottom.

ideas.name: Long XLV vs short XLK
ideas.line: Long XLV / short XLK: 100th pctile vs failing semis
ideas.expr: Long XLV, short equal notional XLK. Express the long side with LLY and IBB if you want more torque.
ideas.thesis: The money evicted from the AI complex is going into drugs and devices with earnings behind it, not into cash. Health care has the strongest relative-strength profile on the sheet (+7.1% 1m, +8.7% 3m, turning up) against technology whose 1-month relative strength is -3.6% and whose semiconductor core is decelerating.

ideas.name: Long ITA (defense catch-up to LMT)
ideas.line: Long ITA: LMT z=3.35 but ITA only 30th pctile
ideas.expr: Buy ITA; or buy Jan ITA 220 calls.
ideas.thesis: The single largest positive score on the entire board is a defense prime, yet the sector ETF is below its 200-day and in the bottom third of its 52-week range after a -13.4% three-month relative stretch. That gap closes upward in a tape that wants non-cyclical, non-AI earnings.

ideas.name: Developed ex-US over EM
ideas.line: LONG EFA / SHORT EEM - LatAm unravels, EM/SPY z=-1.84
ideas.expr: Long EFA, short EEM, equal notional. Cheaper variant: long EWG/EWU basket vs short EWZ.
ideas.thesis: EM's drawdown is concentrated in the currency: Brazil and Mexico are both bleeding through FX while their local indices hold up, which is how real EM dislocations start. Europe is doing the opposite — DAX, EWG and EWU all turning up with the euro firming.

ideas.name: Long SMH / short EWY
ideas.line: Long SMH vs short EWY: the won says the squeeze is over
ideas.expr: Long SMH, short EWY, dollar-neutral at roughly 1:1 notional.
ideas.thesis: Korea's +5.4% day was a short squeeze financed by a weakening currency, and it has already given back. You keep the silicon exposure where the cycle still works and short the leveraged, FX-exposed version of it. KOSPI's one-month move is z=-1.94 at -13.6% while SMH/SPY is turning up off a z=-1.2.

ideas.name: Short Coinbase
ideas.line: Short COIN: crypto bleeding while SPX sits at 95th pct
ideas.expr: Short COIN outright or buy January 160/120 put spread.
ideas.thesis: Crypto is the highest-beta read on retail risk appetite and it is decaying while the index makes highs — exactly the divergence that preceded past drawdowns in speculative beta. COIN carries the volume-decline and the equity-beta risk at once: -54.3% over twelve months, 9.9th percentile, rolling over, relative strength -16.1% on the month.

ideas.name: Silicon over electrons
ideas.line: PAIR: long SMH vs short GEV/ETN/NLR power basket
ideas.expr: Long SMH against an equal-dollar short basket of GEV, ETN and NLR (optionally add GRID and VST), roughly 1:1 notional.
ideas.thesis: The AI capex dollar is rotating out of the power build-out and back into the chips. The electricity complex is making 52-week lows with negative acceleration while semis are re-accelerating off a washout — the same money, a different leg.

ideas.name: Steepener equity expression: banks over bond proxies
ideas.line: PAIR: long XLF vs short XLU — curve beats the yield proxy
ideas.expr: Long XLF (add KRE for more curve beta) against an equal-dollar XLU short.
ideas.thesis: A 38bp 2s10s that just steepened 9bp is net income for banks and a discount-rate problem for utilities. Utilities have rallied 8.3% on the month on a z=1.58 move with acceleration +2.15 while the trend state is still down and 3m relative strength is -10.2% — that is a crowded defensive bid about to meet a 5.37% thirty-year.

ideas.name: Health care and biotech as the new defensive growth
ideas.line: LONG IBB + XLV: rs turning up, XLV at 96th pctile
ideas.expr: Long IBB as the core with an XLV overlay; relative version is long IBB against short XLC, which sits at the 0th percentile with -11.0% 3m relative strength.
ideas.thesis: If the market wants defense, this is the only defensive group with earnings growth and upward relative strength rather than a crowded bond-proxy bid. It also carries zero oil and zero duration sensitivity, which is what today's tape penalised.

ideas.name: Oil services (OIH) as the un-extended way to own $100 crude
ideas.line: Long OIH: $100 WTI, and OIH is only 3% over its 200d
ideas.expr: Buy OIH outright, or Jan OIH 420/470 call spread. Size half the usual energy clip given the sector's run.
ideas.thesis: Energy is the only sector with rising relative strength (+10.2% 1m vs S&P), but XLE is 18.0% above its 200-day at the 95th percentile and XOP is 18.7% extended. OIH is up only 3.9% on the month and sits 3.2% over its 200-day with trend turning up — the catch-up leg, not the crowded one.

ideas.name: Long Taiwan (EWT) vs short Korea (EWY)
ideas.line: Long EWT / short EWY: KOSPI's 6.6% rip isn't confirmed by the won
ideas.expr: Long EWT, short EWY, dollar-neutral. Put it on into the Korean strength.
ideas.thesis: Both are semi beta, so the pair isolates the quality of the move. Taiwan is in an uptrend 15.6% above its 200-day at the 82nd percentile with relative strength rising (+9.6% 3m); Korea is 'rolling over', -15.9% on the month (z=-1.93) and 2.7% below its 200-day. A 6.6% KOSPI session that comes with a 1.1% weaker won is a local squeeze, not foreign allocation.

ideas.name: Long silver vs gold — fade a z=1.63 ratio blowout
ideas.line: Long SLV / short GLD: gold-silver +10.9% in a month, z=1.63
ideas.expr: Long SLV against short GLD, roughly equal notional. Start half size; this is a knife-catch.
ideas.thesis: Gold/silver is +10.9% on the month at a z=1.63 move with acceleration still positive (+1.07) and the 78th percentile of its year, while silver sits 24.6% below its 200-day at the 10th percentile with a z=-1.42 month. The macro backdrop — crude +77% YTD, copper at the 91st percentile, copper/gold at a 52-week high — argues the industrial metal shouldn't be liquidating 12% a month against the monetary one.

ideas.name: Long XLI vs short XLU — unwind the defensive crowd
ideas.line: Long XLI / short XLU: ratio at z=-2.10, XLU acceleration 2.33
ideas.expr: Long XLI, short XLU, equal notional. Or express as long SPHB/short SPLV for the same trade with more convexity.
ideas.thesis: Industrials/utilities is at a z=-2.10 move with acceleration -1.91 — a two-sigma dislocation. Utilities are +8.5% on the month (z=1.63) with the board's second-highest acceleration (+2.33) yet trade 2.1% BELOW their 200-day and at the 48th percentile: that is yield-chasing, not leadership. Meanwhile the growth pulse is turning — transports +5.0% on the month, UPS +12.9%, FDX +7.4%, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54 — and the defensive complex (XLP acc 1.89, SPLV 2.35, USMV 1.57) is maximally crowded.

ideas.name: Short LMT vs long ITA — fade the single-name defense squeeze
ideas.line: Short LMT / long ITA: LMT z=2.59 inside a 15th-pct sector
ideas.expr: Short LMT, long ITA at ~1.5x LMT notional. Or buy Dec LMT 600 puts financed by ITA calls.
ideas.thesis: LMT is +19.9% on the month at a z=2.59 move with the highest acceleration on the board (+2.73) and 10.8% above its 200-day, sitting inside an aerospace & defense sector that is -3.5% on the month, 9.9% below its 200-day, at the 15th percentile and in a downtrend with relative strength -19.1% over three months. Either the sector catches up or the single name gives it back; the pair pays on convergence and hedges a geopolitical escalation.

ideas.name: Beta over defense
ideas.line: Long SPHB vs short SPLV: fade the crowded defensive bid
ideas.expr: Long SPHB / short SPLV, equal dollar. Overlay: sell XLU and XLP against it if you want the sector version.
ideas.thesis: The defensive trade is the most extended thing on the board — SPLV acceleration 2.35, XLU 2.33, XLP 1.89, USMV at the 96th percentile — while high-beta/low-vol washed out to z=-2.0 and turned up today. With MOVE under 100 and VIX at 17.52, the insurance premium that funded that bid is deflating.

ideas.name: Semis relative-strength turn
ideas.line: Long SMH vs SPY: ratio turns up from z=-1.45
ideas.expr: Long SMH vs short SPY, 1:1 notional; or Dec SMH 570/620 call spreads for convexity.
ideas.thesis: The semis drawdown was a positioning flush, not a fundamental break — SMH is still +55% on the year with TSM, AMD and MU all in uptrends. The ratio bottomed at z=-1.45 and has now turned, three sessions into a broadening bounce that today included second-tier names (AVGO +4.0%, ASML +2.8%), not just NVDA.

ideas.name: META as the funding short
ideas.line: Short META: acceleration z=-3.03, XLC at the 0th percentile
ideas.expr: Short META outright, or short META vs long QQQ to isolate the idiosyncratic leg. Options: Dec 600 puts.
ideas.thesis: META has the worst acceleration reading on the entire board at -3.03, is -17.5% on the month and -10.7% on the week, and sits inside the only sector at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range. It fell 1.6% on a day when high beta rose 2.9% — that is distribution, not de-risking.

ideas.name: Transports turn
ideas.line: Long IYT: UPS +5.8%, IYT/SPY acceleration +2.54
ideas.expr: Long IYT, or long an equal-weight version via XTN to avoid single-name concentration; UPS and FDX are the core longs.
ideas.thesis: The cyclical pulse is improving off a very low base. Transports are -9.1% relative to the S&P over three months and IYT/SPY is at the 28th percentile, but the acceleration is the highest in the factor block at +2.54, and the two bellwethers are both making their best moves of the year.

ideas.name: Long duration into the FOMC
ideas.line: Long TLT 81.7 / Dec calls: the impulse is decelerating
ideas.expr: Buy TLT outright at 81.68, or Dec 85 calls for convexity; futures alternative is long TY/US into the statement.
ideas.thesis: Yield levels are still punitive but every acceleration z-score across the curve is deeply negative (2y -2.06, 5y -1.98, 10y -1.92, 10y real -1.97) and the month's changes are -13 to -18bp. Crude cracking removes the Fed's last excuse to sound hawkish. You are paid on a pause plus a dovish second derivative.

ideas.name: Fade the crude-beta extension
ideas.line: Short XOP vs SPY: oil cracked, the equity hasn't marked it
ideas.expr: Short XOP at 204.86 against equal-notional long SPY; or buy XOP December puts ~10% out of the money.
ideas.thesis: Energy equity is priced for a war premium that is actively deflating in Tehran. XOP sits 21.7% above its 200-day at the 100th percentile of its year, +12.9% on the month at z=1.02, XLE 20.6% above its 200-day. This is a mean-reversion of extension, not a structural bear call — XLE's 3m relative strength of +15.6% stays the long-term trend.

ideas.name: Mexico over Brazil
ideas.line: Long EWW vs short EWZ — LatAm dispersion, not LatAm beta
ideas.expr: Equal dollar long EWW / short EWZ, 1% NAV per leg. FX overlay version: long MXN / short BRL 3-month forwards.
ideas.thesis: Today was sovereign repricing, not a dollar squeeze — DXY was +0.2% and USD/KRW and USD/CNY sit at the 0th percentile. A 6.4% one-day currency gap and a 13.9% index drop almost never resolve in a session; positioning unwinds take weeks. Mexico is doing the exact opposite on the same continent.

ideas.name: Short crude on the product crack
ideas.line: Short WTI: gasoline -7.9% on the month is leading crude lower
ideas.expr: Short front-month WTI futures, or buy December $95 puts for ~50bp premium. Keep XLE long as a partial offset if you own energy equity.
ideas.thesis: Refined products turn before crude. Crude is 18.3% above its 200-day and +76.5% YTD on an inflation bid, and it is the single input keeping the rates composite at -42 and the inflation composite at -47. Breaking it is the cheapest way to get everything else easier.

ideas.name: Sell the discretionary bounce
ideas.line: Long XLP vs short XLY — fade today's +1.4% ratio pop
ideas.expr: Long XLP / short XLY, equal dollars, 1.5% NAV per leg. Single-name version: long WMT and COST versus short XLY.
ideas.thesis: The defensive bid is the fastest-accelerating thing in the US tape while the index grinds sideways. XLY/XLP sits at the 6th percentile of its year in a confirmed downtrend; a 1.4% one-day bounce in a ratio that deep in a downtrend is an entry, not a turn.

ideas.name: Short comm services
ideas.line: Short XLC: 0th percentile, META acceleration -2.95
ideas.expr: Short XLC, or buy November META puts ~5% OTM; pair against long SPY to strip out index beta.
ideas.thesis: Comm services is the only sector making 52-week lows while the S&P sits in the 90th percentile — the market is repricing ad and streaming economics against AI capex, and that is a multi-quarter de-rating, not a dip.

ideas.name: Belly duration via IEF
ideas.line: Long IEF: Brent -6% gives the curve its first excuse
ideas.expr: Buy IEF outright, or 5-year note futures (FVZ6); size to ~1.5x normal because the 2-year is doing the work. Overlay: sell 10y 5.25% strike risk via a payer spread if you want carry.
ideas.thesis: Crude has been the only thing driving the rates composite to -44. Brent -6.0% and gasoline -8.5% on the month at z=-0.90 remove the marginal inflation bid just as the curve's upward acceleration collapses.

ideas.name: Short HYG / long LQD
ideas.line: Short junk vs IG: HYG 36th pctile, SPX 87th
ideas.expr: Short HYG, long LQD dollar-for-dollar (duration-light credit-quality pair). Alternative: buy HYG Dec 76 puts.
ideas.thesis: The AI capex-debt story is leaking into high yield before it shows in equities. HYG/IEF is -2.2% on the month at z=-1.63 with acceleration -1.32 while the S&P sits at the 87th percentile of its range — that gap closes down, not up.

ideas.name: Long IGV / short SMH
ideas.line: Software over semis: IGV/SMH z=2.42, still 39th pctile
ideas.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal notional. Express the tail with SMH Dec puts against long IGV stock.
ideas.thesis: The AI trade is being re-sorted, not abandoned: capital is leaving the memory/hardware leg and funding software and security. The ratio has moved 33.8% in a quarter yet still sits in the 39th percentile of its own 52-week range, so this is early in a mean reversion, not late in a momentum chase.

ideas.name: Oil services catch-up vs E&P
ideas.line: Long OIH vs short XOP — services haven't marked $103 crude
ideas.expr: Long OIH, short XOP, dollar-neutral, sized to roughly 1.0x beta on the ratio.
ideas.thesis: E&P has fully priced $100 crude; the service complex has not. XOP is +10.4% on the month, 20.4% above its 200-day and at the 100th percentile of its year, while OIH is +0.4% on the month and 0.6% above its 200-day at the 69th percentile. If crude holds here, activity budgets follow and the laggard closes the gap; if crude breaks, you own the cheaper leg.

ideas.name: Fade the crowded staples bid
ideas.line: Short XLP vs SPY: the defensive hideout just cracked
ideas.expr: Short XLP, long an equal dollar amount of SPY. Options version: buy XLP Dec puts, sell SPY Dec puts of equal premium.
ideas.thesis: Staples became the consensus hiding place: +7.1% on the month, +8.2% relative to the S&P, z=1.80 with acceleration 2.21, 89th percentile. That is a bond proxy bought on a rate-cut assumption that just got withdrawn, with a 10-year at 5.00% and a December hike live. Crowded defensives unwind faster than they accumulate.

ideas.name: Tactical semiconductor bounce
ideas.line: Long SMH: first semi leadership day off a z=-1.8 washout
ideas.expr: Long SMH at 527, or December 540/600 call spread to cap risk on a counter-trend trade.
ideas.thesis: The semi de-rating has been the dominant 2026 Q4 trade — SOXX -15.5% on the month at z=-1.83 with acceleration -1.93 — and it is now mature enough to produce a violent squeeze. Crucially SMH is still 2.4% above its 200-day and in an up trend; this is a de-rating of multiple, not a break of the price cycle.

ideas.name: Healthcare leadership
ideas.line: LONG XLV - 100th pctile, RS +8% on the month, accel 1.63
ideas.expr: Buy XLV; barbell the single names with equal-weight LLY and UNH for the high-beta version.
ideas.thesis: Healthcare is the only sector combining 52-week-high price, accelerating relative strength and defensive cash flows. In a tape de-rating growth multiples while nominal GDP stays hot, this is where the index-level money relocates.

ideas.name: Low-vol over high-beta
ideas.line: Long SPLV vs short SPHB - the beta unwind is accelerating
ideas.expr: Long SPLV, short SPHB, dollar-neutral. Size the short slightly smaller for beta, or substitute USMV long vs QQQ short for a more liquid version.
ideas.thesis: The index is being hollowed out from the top: defensives and equal-weight absorb the flows while high-beta, momentum and growth are liquidated. This rotation is being driven by a de-rating of the AI capex complex, not by a credit or macro event, so it can run for weeks without the index collapsing.

ideas.name: Brazil over China
ideas.line: Long EWZ / short FXI: Brazil 93rd pctile, China 15th
ideas.expr: Long EWZ vs short FXI, dollar-neutral; add KWEB to the short leg for higher beta.
ideas.thesis: Brazil is the one EM that benefits from $112 Brent with a firming currency, and it is already trending. China is a falling knife with a weakening index and no currency offset. Inside a deteriorating EEM/SPY, you want to be long the terms-of-trade winner and short the loser rather than long the aggregate.

ideas.name: Short MSTR vs long IBIT
ideas.line: Short MSTR vs long IBIT: +7.5% on a day BTC fell 2.6%
ideas.expr: Short MSTR vs long IBIT at equal dollar notional; or buy MSTR January puts outright if borrow is expensive.
ideas.thesis: The levered bitcoin proxy rallied 7.5% into a tape where the underlying fell. That gap is premium-to-NAV expansion on a name down 49% year on year, with no spot support. Own the clean exposure, short the financing structure.

ideas.name: Long health care vs short communications
ideas.line: Long XLV / short XLC: strongest relative accel vs the only broken sector
ideas.expr: Long XLV, short XLC, dollar-neutral. Single-name overlay: long LLY/UNH, short NFLX.
ideas.thesis: Defensive leadership is not fading - it is accelerating - and communications is the sector where the fundamental damage is single-name and still unfolding. XLV relative strength is +5.9% on the month with acceleration z=1.57 at the 97.7th percentile; XLC is -5.0% on the month at the 28th percentile with acceleration z=-1.13.

ideas.name: Long Brent vs short WTI
ideas.line: Long Brent vs short WTI: the $10.9 spread is widening again
ideas.expr: Long ICE Brent Dec/Jan futures vs short equal-barrel CME WTI, 1:1; retail proxy long BNO / short USO.
ideas.thesis: The waterborne barrel is bid and the landlocked one isn't. Brent is +9.8% on the month (z=0.75, 86th percentile) with positive acceleration (+0.25); WTI is +3.6% with acceleration -0.39. A dislocation this wide normally mean-reverts via WTI catching up, but with WTI selling 2.5% on a day Brent rallies, the physical tightness is offshore.

ideas.name: Health care relative to the index
ideas.line: Long XLV vs SPY: acc z=2.05, 100th pctile, rs +6.2% 1m
ideas.expr: Long XLV (or 50/50 LLY+UNH) against equal-notional short SPY; add IBB for the biotech kicker.
ideas.thesis: This is the only leadership group on the tape with trend, acceleration, and relative strength all pointing the same way. Defensive leadership is a poor signal for the index but an excellent one for a relative-value book, and it is where the money leaving AI is actually landing.

ideas.name: AI-power derivative complex
ideas.line: Short GEV and the nuclear/grid complex: no bid, 0th percentile
ideas.expr: Short GEV outright (or Jan puts ~10% OTM), paired with a short in NLR; keep ETN and CEG on the same leash.
ideas.thesis: The power-for-AI trade is being unwound by the same money that is selling semis, and it has no valuation floor and no natural buyer. Every leg of the complex is in a down or rolling-over trend with 52-week percentiles at or near zero.

ideas.name: Short the AI-power complex (GEV)
ideas.line: Short GEV / NLR: power chain down 11-13% with no bid
ideas.expr: Short GEV outright, or buy 3-month GEV puts ~10% out of the money. Basket alternative: equal-weight short GEV, ETN, CEG, VST; add NLR for the nuclear leg. Keep it small — these are high-beta, high-borrow names.
ideas.thesis: The second-derivative AI trade — power generation, grid, nuclear fuel, rare earths — is being liquidated outright, not rotated. These are the names that got priced on a datacenter capex curve that semis are now questioning. The complex is breaking to new 52-week lows while the index is up, which is how real distribution looks.

ideas.name: Long RSP / short QQQ
ideas.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ: breadth acc z=1.70, QQQ/SPY -1.4% 1m
ideas.expr: Buy RSP, short QQQ, equal dollars. Size at roughly 1:1 — RSP's realized beta to the pair is lower, so expect slow grind rather than a spike.
ideas.thesis: The rate shock that crushed everything outside mega-cap tech is easing at the long end exactly as the semis complex rolls. That is the setup for equal-weight to close its gap to cap-weight. The breadth acceleration print is the strongest confirmation signal on the board.

ideas.name: Short XOP into the crude break
ideas.line: Short XOP: 99.6th pctile, +20% over 200d, WTI just lost $100
ideas.expr: Short XOP, or buy XOP 2-month puts. Hedge the geopolitical gap risk by owning a small Brent call spread against it — the Brent-WTI spread at ~$10.9 is where the supply premium actually lives.
ideas.thesis: Energy equities are priced for a sustained triple-digit WTI that just evaporated in one session. XOP sits at the 99.6th percentile of its 52-week range and 20.1% above its 200-day; XLE is at the 99th. The crude move was a seaborne supply premium, not demand — gasoline and grains say the inflation impulse is already rolling over.

ideas.name: Short Korea (EWY)
ideas.line: Short EWY: Korea's AI unwind is accelerating, not bottoming
ideas.expr: Short EWY outright, or buy Dec EWY puts ~10% OTM. Fade into any 3-5% bounce; keep size modest given the -19.5% month already behind us.
ideas.thesis: The memory/AI-capex trade is unwinding at a pace with no precedent on this tape, and Monday's +4.1% EWY pop was a positioning bounce that lasted one session. With KOSPI still only at the 32.8th percentile of its 52-week range after a 19.5% monthly fall, there is room below.

ideas.name: Short high-yield credit via HYG puts
ideas.line: Buy HYG puts: loans at z=-1.36 while VIX fell 7.8%
ideas.expr: Buy Dec/Jan HYG 75 puts, funded by selling 79 calls; or short BKLN outright for the cleaner, less-hedged expression.
ideas.thesis: Credit is the one market that refused to take the equity bounce. Loans — the most senior, most floating-rate part of the stack — are the weakest z-score on the tape, which says it is cash-flow coverage at 5%+ front-end rates, not duration. Equity vol is now cheap enough to hedge this asymmetrically.

ideas.name: Long QUAL vs short SPHB
ideas.line: Fade the beta squeeze: QUAL long, SPHB short
ideas.expr: Long QUAL, short SPHB, equal dollar notional.
ideas.thesis: Today's rally was a short-cover in the most levered, lowest-quality cohort while the broad tape fell. High beta/low vol is still in a month-long downtrend (z=-1.10, acc z=-1.03) and breadth is deteriorating — the regime favors balance-sheet quality, which is accelerating, not beta.

ideas.name: Long XLE / short XLI
ideas.line: Long XLE vs short XLI: 100th pctile vs rolling over
ideas.expr: Dollar-neutral long XLE against short XLI; or express the long leg via XOM/CVX and short XLI against it.
ideas.thesis: Energy is the only sector at the 100th percentile of its 52-week range with relative strength still rising, and it held that on a day crude fell 2.7% — cash flow, not spot oil, is driving it. Industrials are the mirror: rolling over, -8.9% relative over three months.

ideas.name: Long Korea (EWY)
ideas.line: Long EWY: -16% month, z=-2.35, won at 52wk strong
ideas.expr: Long EWY, or KOSPI futures; hedge the beta with a partial SMH short if you only want the Asia-vs-US-semi relative.
ideas.thesis: A -16.3% monthly drawdown at z=-2.35 with acceleration z=-2.24 is capitulation, not a slow de-rating, and the currency refuses to confirm distress. When the exchange rate is at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range (i.e. strongest) during an equity rout, you are looking at a de-grossing, not an exit.

ideas.name: Short USDMXN
ideas.line: Short USDMXN: z=2.81 blowout, equities disagree
ideas.expr: Short USDMXN in forwards, 1-2% risk budget; or buy 3-month USDMXN puts to cap the tail if this is a policy/fiscal event rather than a flow unwind.
ideas.thesis: A 7.6% monthly move at z=2.81 with acceleration z=1.69 is the most extreme reading in the entire digest, and nothing around it corroborates: CEW is -0.3% on the month, USDBRL -1.0%, USDKRW -3.7%. Mexican equities are making highs, not discounting a shock.

ideas.name: Energy over the index
ideas.line: Long XLE vs SPY: crude breakout, energy at 52-week highs
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XLE (use XOP for the higher-beta sleeve) versus short SPY. Add XOM/CVX as single-name expression for the dividend-anchored version.
ideas.thesis: Oil is the one macro variable reasserting itself. Brent at 109.69 (+80.3% ytd) with producers at the 100th percentile of their range and relative strength still rising means energy earnings revisions lead the index, and it hedges the breakeven risk embedded in everything else in the book.

ideas.name: Nasdaq downside convexity
ideas.line: QQQ put spread: vol curve flat, tails already bid
ideas.expr: Buy a December QQQ put spread roughly 4% / 11% out of the money. With SKEW at the 100th percentile the far wing is rich — sell it, own the near strike. Do not buy naked wings.
ideas.thesis: The semis and high-beta unwind is a week old and only partially done: QQQ is still 5.4% above its 200-day and SMH 5.6% above its. With the VIX curve flat, near-dated protection carries almost nothing, which is rare.

ideas.name: Brazil over EM
ideas.line: Long EWZ vs short EEM: Brazil is the EM that works
ideas.expr: Long EWZ versus short EEM, equal dollars. Unhedged — the BRL leg is part of the trade.
ideas.thesis: EM is splitting. Brazil combines a commodity bid (Brent, copper), a firming currency and domestic momentum; the EM index is dominated by the Korea/Taiwan semis unwind. Own the divergence rather than the aggregate.

ideas.name: Big pharma over small biotech
ideas.line: Long XLV vs short XBI: cash flow over long duration
ideas.expr: Long XLV (or a basket of LLY and UNH) versus short XBI, equal dollars.
ideas.thesis: With the 10y at 5.09% and real yields at 2.74%, unprofitable long-duration biotech is the wrong side of both the rate and the vol regime, while large-cap healthcare is the only sector whose relative strength is actually turning up.

ideas.name: Copper over gold
ideas.line: Long FCX vs short GLD - copper/gold at 94th pctile
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long FCX (or Dec HG copper futures) against short GLD. Scale 1:1 notional; FCX is the higher-beta leg, so half-size it if running the futures version.
ideas.thesis: The portfolio hedge is rotating from the fear metal to the growth metal. Copper is backed by a falling dollar and a 33.8% year-over-year price; gold has lost its real-yield sponsor with 10y TIPS at 2.78% and no crisis bid showing up in credit.

ideas.name: Crypto beta on the dollar break
ideas.line: Long IBIT with a COIN kicker - BTC +8.4% 1m, trend turning up
ideas.expr: Long IBIT as the core, 2:1 against a smaller COIN position for torque. Size to 1-1.5% of NAV given realized vol.
ideas.thesis: The highest-beta liquidity gauge turned before anything else and is doing so against a falling dollar from deeply washed-out percentiles — the classic setup for a multi-week catch-up rather than a dead-cat bounce.

ideas.name: Long XLV / short XLF
ideas.line: Long XLV vs short XLF - only clean sector trend vs a broken one
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV / short XLF. Higher-beta version: long LLY + UNH vs short KRE.
ideas.thesis: Health care is the only sector with price, momentum and relative strength all aligned, and it is working without the market's help. Financials' relative strength is rolling over with the curve flat at 33bp and regional banks at the 22nd percentile versus the S&P.

ideas.name: Fade E&P beta, keep the majors
ideas.line: Short XOP / long XOM as crude accelerates lower
ideas.expr: Short XOP (or buy Dec XOP puts), long XOM against it, roughly 1:1 dollar. Size 1/3 of a full position given energy's momentum.
ideas.thesis: Energy equities are priced at the top of their 52-week range while the barrel is falling fast. E&P beta carries the highest operating leverage to a $94 WTI print and a collapsing crack; XOM is the quality anchor with relative strength still turning up, so the pair isolates the de-rating without fighting the sector's cash returns.

ideas.name: Korea capitulation bounce
ideas.line: Small long EWY vs short EWT into a 2.35-sigma flush
ideas.expr: Buy EWY November calls or a small cash long, hedged with a short in EWT; quarter-size, add only on stabilisation.
ideas.thesis: A 7.6% single-day index drop with a z of -2.35 is liquidation, not information. The won has not broken (USDKRW still -9.5% over three months) and Taiwan, the other half of the same supply chain, is up 3.2% on the month with relative strength up — the dislocation is positioning-driven and should partly reverse.

ideas.name: Long health care vs short semis
ideas.line: Long XLV / short SMH - defensives over silicon
ideas.expr: Buy XLV, short SMH dollar-neutral (roughly 1:1 notional). Options version: XLV Dec calls funded by SMH Dec call sales.
ideas.thesis: Today the market stopped paying for AI capex and started paying for cash flow. XLV has the strongest relative-strength trend in the sector table (turning up, +2.7% 1m, +7.9% 3m) at the 97th percentile, while semis are unwinding a parabolic move with the entire supply chain breaking together. A rate backdrop where the front end prices hikes punishes long-duration equity and rewards defensives.

ideas.name: Short the AI-power build-out complex
ideas.line: Short VST/CEG/GEV basket - capex trade is unwinding
ideas.expr: Equal-weight short basket of VST, CEG and GEV; add GRID or NLR as a tail leg. Hedge with a small long in XLU to isolate the capex premium.
ideas.thesis: The power/electrification complex was priced on an uninterrupted AI build. With chips de-rating and financing costs re-accelerating at the front end, the terminal-demand assumption is the first thing repriced. These names have the highest beta to that assumption.

ideas.name: Long energy vs short metals & mining
ideas.line: Long XLE / short XME - the only cyclical still bid
ideas.expr: Long XLE (or an XOM/CVX pair), short XME, dollar-neutral.
ideas.thesis: Energy is the single sector with price, earnings and relative strength all working, and it is the one that benefits from the crude-side bid that is driving the index's real-yield problem. Mining is the opposite: it is long the dollar-sensitive metals that got liquidated today and has no cash-flow story at these rates.

ideas.name: 2s10s flattener
ideas.line: Pay 2y, receive 10y - curve re-flattening on CPI
ideas.expr: Short 2-year Treasury futures (TU) against long 10-year futures (TY), DV01-neutral.
ideas.thesis: The consensus steepener assumed cuts. A hot CPI with the front end at 52-week highs and the long end rallying on growth doubt inverts that logic. The curve flattens from both ends in this regime.

ideas.name: Long XOP vs short IWM
ideas.line: Long XOP vs short IWM: oil's third leg vs rate-squeezed smalls
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XOP, short IWM. Cash ETFs or XLE/Russell-future variant for size; rebalance weekly to equal notional.
ideas.thesis: Crude is the one asset still tightening financial conditions and it pays the producer directly, while small caps carry the cost of a 5.21% 10-year, a 7.40% mortgage and no front-end relief. The pair harvests both ends of the same shock.

ideas.name: Long XOP / short JETS
ideas.line: Long XOP vs short JETS: crude back up 5.8% on the week
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar pair: long XOP, short JETS. Size 1.0x/1.0x; roll monthly.
ideas.thesis: Crude round-tripped the entire relief move while the fuel-consumer complex is already in a downtrend. Producers are at new highs with the best relative strength in the book; airlines are the purest short-side expression of a $95 barrel.

ideas.name: Short regional banks (KRE)
ideas.line: Short KRE into earnings: KRE/SPY at the 14th percentile
ideas.expr: Short KRE outright, or buy Dec 68/60 put spreads; hedge beta with a half-size SPY long if you want the pure relative.
ideas.thesis: Banks go into earnings already marked down, the curve is flattening again rather than steepening into their margins, and the alt/broker complex is breaking first — the classic sequence before credit-sensitive lenders get repriced.

ideas.name: Long FCX / short GDX
ideas.line: Long copper equity vs short gold miners: Cu/Au 100th pctile
ideas.expr: Long FCX (add COPX for breadth), short GDX, equal dollars.
ideas.thesis: Copper/gold at the 100th percentile with the metal at the 96th while the precious complex is in an outright downtrend. Gold miners carry the most negative acceleration in the industry book and are losing to their own underlying.

ideas.name: Energy equity vs the barrel
ideas.line: Short XLE: energy equities at 100th pctile, barrel rolling
ideas.expr: Short XLE or buy December 63-strike XLE puts; purer version is short XOP against a small long in crude futures.
ideas.thesis: Energy equities are priced at the 52-week high while the commodity that pays for them has turned. Gasoline cracking is the tell that the product side, not just crude, is loosening — refining and E&P cash flows roll with a lag the equity hasn't taken.

ideas.name: Regional banks into earnings (KRE vs SPY)
ideas.line: Short KRE vs long SPY: curve flattening, relative strength 13th pctile
ideas.expr: Short KRE against an equal-dollar long SPY; or buy KRE November put spreads ahead of the money-center prints.
ideas.thesis: Banks are not getting the steepener they need, loan demand is being killed by a 7.40% mortgage and a 2.91% real yield, and the capital-markets complex is already telling you fees are missing. Relative strength is broken before earnings, not after.

ideas.name: Healthcare over discretionary (XLV vs XLY)
ideas.line: Long XLV / short XLY: new leadership vs a credit-starved consumer
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV, short XLY; higher-beta version is long IBB vs short XRT.
ideas.thesis: Healthcare is the only new sector whose relative strength is turning up, with earnings-driven large caps leading. Discretionary is levered to exactly the thing that is tightening — mortgage rates, real yields and a dollar at a 100th-percentile print squeezing the goods consumer.

ideas.name: Long software/cyber vs short semis
ideas.line: Long IGV+CIBR vs short SMH: code is eating silicon's bid
ideas.expr: Long equal notional IGV and CIBR versus short SMH, dollar-neutral, rebalanced weekly. Cash equity or swap.
ideas.thesis: With real yields at 2.91% and rising, capital is rotating from capex-heavy, cyclically-priced silicon into cash-generative software and security spend that does not need a weaker dollar or cheaper debt. CIBR's acceleration z of 2.29 at the 100th percentile with z=2.11 is the strongest trending series in the digest.

ideas.name: Long healthcare vs short banks
ideas.line: Long XLV vs short KBE: new leadership vs the persistent leak
ideas.expr: Long XLV (add IBB for beta) versus short KBE or KRE, equal notional.
ideas.thesis: Healthcare is the only new sector leadership in the tape, broad across large biotech, small biotech and managed care. Banks are the one group that cannot catch a bid even on green days: the 2-year at 4.80% (+37bp on the month) raises funding costs while 2s10s flattened 3bp today, and the capital-markets complex is in outright drawdown.

ideas.name: Short the capex periphery
ideas.line: Short DE and PAVE: the machinery cycle is cracking
ideas.expr: Short DE outright or via 3-month puts; pair with a short in PAVE against long SPY if you want sector-neutrality.
ideas.thesis: Falling crop prices plus 7%+ financing costs plus a record dollar is the worst possible mix for farm and heavy equipment. Industrials relative strength is already in a downtrend and the infrastructure/capex basket is quietly failing while the index makes highs.

ideas.name: Short EM beta against the S&P on the dollar squeeze
ideas.line: Short EEM vs long SPY: dollar acceleration hits EM first
ideas.expr: Short EEM, long equal-notional SPY. Overlay: long USD vs MXN 3-month forward for the pure FX leg.
ideas.thesis: Tightening has migrated from the curve to the currency. A dollar at the 98th percentile and still accelerating is a direct hit to EM earnings, funding and flows, and the relative series are already breaking before the headline index does.

ideas.name: Long software vs short semis
ideas.line: Long IGV vs short SMH: software over capex-heavy semis
ideas.expr: Equal dollar notional: long IGV, short SMH (or SOXX). Roughly 1.0 beta-matched; size 3-5% of book per leg.
ideas.thesis: The market is paying for software that funds itself out of cash flow and discounting anything that requires capex, power and foreign fabs. Semis carry the highest extension on the board; software carries the acceleration.

ideas.name: AI cash flow over AI debt
ideas.line: Short ORCL vs long MSFT: AI debt vs AI cash flow
ideas.expr: Short ORCL, long MSFT, equal dollar notional. Express the short with Jan puts if borrow is expensive.
ideas.thesis: The market has begun to separate hyperscalers funding AI out of operating cash flow from those funding it with balance sheet. ORCL is the purest listed proxy for levered AI capex and it is being repriced as a credit, not an equity.

ideas.name: Short India equity
ideas.line: Short INDA: INR near 99th pctile, Sensex -14.8% YTD
ideas.expr: Short INDA, 2% position, or buy 3-month puts. Keep it small — it is a trend-follow, not a valuation call.
ideas.thesis: India is losing on both the currency and the index, and the currency weakness is accelerating rather than stabilising. There is no local catalyst to arrest a trend this entrenched while the dollar composite is still firm.

ideas.name: Long XOP vs short SPY
ideas.line: Long XOP vs SPY: crude +4.4%, energy equity hasn't marked it
ideas.expr: Buy XOP, short equal-notional SPY. Cash-equity version: long XOM/CVX basket vs SPY. Avoid OIH — services are rolling over (-10.8% on the month, acc -1.29).
ideas.thesis: Today's 4.4% move in both WTI and Brent happened after US energy equities last printed. Brent at 104.59 is +37.1% on three months with XLE's one-month relative strength at just -1.6% and XOP's at -2.0%. Equity has not discounted a $104 Brent; the three-month relative trends (XLE +9.7%, XOP +11.6%) say it eventually does.

ideas.name: Short IAI vs long XLV
ideas.line: Short IAI vs long XLV: capital markets crack, defensives bid
ideas.expr: Short IAI (brokers/exchanges), long XLV equal-notional. More aggressive single-name expression: short BX versus long LLY.
ideas.thesis: The capital-markets complex is where the long end is now biting hardest: fee pipelines, mark-to-market books and leveraged balance sheets all reprice to a 5.67% 30-year. Health care is the defensive that is actually bid, with its relative trend turning up, and it has no oil-cost or funding-cost exposure.

ideas.name: Long XLV / short XLI
ideas.line: Long health care, short industrials: defensives w/o duration
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV / short XLI. Concentrated version: long LLY, short CAT.
ideas.thesis: Industrials carry capex, backlog and rate sensitivity into a 5.67% 30-year; today's tape confirmed the unwind has started in the biggest names. Health care gives you defense without the bond proxy problem that is killing utilities and REITs.

ideas.name: Long VST (gas-fired power) / short URA
ideas.line: Long VST vs short uranium: electrons now, fuel stories later
ideas.expr: Long VST (add CEG for diversification) against a short URA leg of equal dollars.
ideas.thesis: The power-demand trade is bifurcating: cash-generating merchant generators are being bid while the speculative fuel-cycle names are being liquidated with the rest of the high-duration complex. Own the cash flows, short the story.

ideas.name: Long Brazil vs short India
ideas.line: EWZ over INDA — the FX decides the EM winner
ideas.expr: Long EWZ, short INDA, equal notional. Scale in on EWZ pullbacks toward 41 given it is 18% above its 200-day.
ideas.thesis: EM is splitting along currencies, not along growth. BRL strength is funding a genuine index breakout; INR weakness at a 99th-percentile USDINR is bleeding Indian equity in dollars.

ideas.name: Short MSTR as the crypto-beta fade
ideas.line: Short MSTR: +69% in 3m into a rising dollar and ETH -4.6%
ideas.expr: Short MSTR outright, or buy Nov/Dec puts ~10% OTM to cap the squeeze risk. Hedge with a small long IBIT if you want pure premium-to-NAV exposure.
ideas.thesis: The crypto bounce was a weak-dollar, falling-real-yield trade. Both have reversed this week, and the leveraged proxy carries three times the beta of the underlying.

ideas.name: Long copper miners vs short gold miners
ideas.line: Long COPX / short GDX: copper-gold at the 98th percentile
ideas.expr: Long COPX, short GDX, dollar-neutral. Alternative single-name version: long FCX vs short NEM.
ideas.thesis: The metals complex is splitting. Copper is +1.0% on the day, +7.8% on three months, at the 92nd percentile, and copper/gold is +7.7% on the month with acceleration 1.32 at the 98th percentile. Gold is -6.4% on the month with z=-1.58 and the miners are unwinding faster than the metal: GDX -11.1% on the month with acceleration -2.04, GDX/gold acceleration -2.06. Falling real-rate hedging demand hurts the gold trade; electrification demand supports the copper trade.

ideas.name: Long cybersecurity (CIBR)
ideas.line: Long CIBR: +14.3% 1m, acceleration 1.77, 100th percentile
ideas.expr: Long CIBR outright, or long CIBR / short QQQ to isolate the relative leg. Buy pullbacks toward the 20-day; do not chase above +3% from spot.
ideas.thesis: This is the cleanest accelerating uptrend on the page that isn't a semiconductor. CIBR is +2.0% on the day, +14.3% on the month, +51.7% YTD, at the 100th percentile with acceleration 1.77 and relative strength of +12.7% (1m) and +12.3% (3m) versus the S&P. With semis stalling today (SMH -0.2%, TSM -0.7%, MU -1.7%) and IGV/SMH +1.5%, software-adjacent spend is where the tech bid is rotating.

ideas.name: Long nuclear/power rebound (NLR)
ideas.line: Long NLR after the squeeze: CEG +12%, VST +11% in one day
ideas.expr: Long NLR with a tight stop; higher-beta expression via CEG or VST, higher-quality via GEV or ETN. Half size — this is a mean-reversion trade in a downtrend.
ideas.thesis: The power complex capitulated into October — NLR -8.8% on the month at the 10.9th percentile and 15.1% below its 200-day, URA -9.2%, CEG flat on the month after a -14.6% year. Today's move was not a drift: CEG +12.2%, VST +10.8%, NLR +5.5%, GEV +4.0%, URA +4.0%. With GRID turning up (acceleration 0.80) and ETN acceleration 1.41, the underlying electricity-demand trade never broke — the financing cost did, and bond vol just cracked lower.

ideas.name: Long S&P vs short Russell 2000
ideas.line: Long SPY / short IWM: IWM/SPY -6% on the month, new lows
ideas.expr: Long SPY, short IWM, dollar-neutral, ~1:1 notional. Or sell IWM call spreads against long SPY.
ideas.thesis: Small caps need lower front-end rates and better credit access; they are getting neither. The 3-month bill is +30bp on the month to 4.21% at the 89th percentile and the 2-year is +42bp — the policy curve is pricing tightening, not easing. IWM/SPY is -6.0% on the month with z=-1.66, down 1.3% today, and regional banks (the Russell's largest financing channel) are at the 20th percentile relative to the S&P with KRE/SPY -7.7% on the month.

ideas.name: Long USDCAD
ideas.line: Long USDCAD: oil breaking, z=1.93 and accelerating at 99th pct
ideas.expr: Long USDCAD spot (short CME CAD futures), or 3-month 1.45 USD calls; size 1x so the carry cost is tolerable.
ideas.thesis: Canada is the cleanest liquid short against falling crude plus a Fed that is still hiking. The rate differential is moving against CAD at the same moment the terms of trade deteriorate, and the trend is already confirmed rather than hopeful.

ideas.name: Long EWZ / short EWW
ideas.line: Long EWZ / short EWW: Brazil re-rates, Mexico bleeds
ideas.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, dollar-neutral. Given EWZ is 18.4% above its 200-day, take half the long via November call spreads rather than cash into the 25 October runoff.
ideas.thesis: One country is re-rating on politics while its neighbour carries the full weight of US rate and trade stress. The currency leg confirms both sides, which is what separates this from a chase.

ideas.name: Brazil into the 25 October runoff
ideas.line: Long EWZ call spread into the Oct 25 runoff
ideas.expr: Buy EWZ Dec 44/52 call spreads rather than stock — the runoff on 25 October is binary and implied vol is cheaper than the realised 12.5% one-day move. Hedge FX exposure is already embedded.
ideas.thesis: Brazil is re-rating on politics with the currency and the index moving together — the cleanest combination in EM. A call spread owns the second leg of the re-rating while capping the loss if the runoff reverses the first round.

ideas.name: Semis over brokers
ideas.line: Long SMH / short IAI: AI vs financial liquidation
ideas.expr: Long SMH, short an equal dollar amount of IAI. Rebalance monthly. Express the short via IAI rather than XLF to avoid the regional-bank squeeze risk.
ideas.thesis: The tape is splitting along the discount rate: cash-generative AI capex compounders versus balance-sheet and fee businesses that need lower vol and tighter spreads. Bond vol at z=3.07 keeps capital markets shut; semis don't care.

ideas.name: Long HYG vs short LQD
ideas.line: Long HYG / short LQD — own the spread, not the duration
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long HYG, short LQD. Institutional version: long CDX HY risk vs short IG duration via 10y futures.
ideas.thesis: The bond selloff is a real-rate event, not a credit event. LQD's damage is pure duration; HY's spread component is still the strongest part of the risk complex. This isolates the part that's working and shorts the part that only loses when the 10y rises.

ideas.name: Long semis vs short equal-weight
ideas.line: Long SMH / short RSP — narrowness is accelerating, not fading
ideas.expr: Buy SMH (or SOXX), short RSP in equal dollars, ~1.0x beta-adjusted; or buy SMH 3-month 25-delta calls funded by RSP downside.
ideas.thesis: The index is being carried by one theme. SMH/SPY z=1.94 with acceleration 1.53 and SOXX +18.2% on the month, against RSP/SPY at the 3.6th percentile of 52 weeks. With 10y real yields at z=1.72 the median S&P name has no multiple support while the AI capex complex has its own earnings cycle (Micron, Korean exports). Own the leadership and fund it with the thing that keeps making new relative lows.

ideas.name: Electrical equipment over power generators
ideas.line: Long ETN+GRID / short CEG+NLR — picks over the power price
ideas.expr: Long 50% ETN / 50% GRID against short 50% CEG / 50% NLR, dollar neutral.
ideas.thesis: AI electrification spend is still being paid for in equipment, not in merchant power. ETN is +12.7% on the month with acceleration 2.02, GRID +4.2% and turning up, GEV +7.2%. The generation side has deflated: CEG -12.6% on the month, NLR -12.1% and at the 0.3rd percentile of 52 weeks, VST at the 4th, URA -10.1%. Falling power-price expectations hit the IPPs and barely touch the backlog names.

ideas.name: Brazil over Mexico
ideas.line: Long EWZ / short EWW — peso stress at z=2.7, Bovespa at 81st
ideas.expr: Long EWZ, short EWW, dollar neutral; size half and add on any EWW bounce toward its 50-day.
ideas.thesis: Mexico is the epicentre of the dollar squeeze: USDMXN z=2.72 with acceleration 2.20, EWW -8.1% on the month, rolling over, relative strength -8.9%/-10.5%. Brazil is the opposite tape — BVSP +2.2% on the week at the 81st percentile, EWZ +8.4% over three months with positive 3-month relative strength, and carry still intact. One LatAm book, two opposite directions.

ideas.name: Short the capital-markets complex
ideas.line: Short BX and IAI — steep curve, still liquidating
ideas.expr: Short BX outright; add short IAI as the diversified leg, or buy BX 3-month puts.
ideas.thesis: The 3m10y curve is at the 98th percentile of the year, the classic green light for financials, and the group keeps being sold anyway: XLF -7.1% on the month with relative strength -7.9%, BX -16.9% (z=-1.76, 22nd percentile), GS -10.3%, IAI -7.6%, KIE z=-1.81. Private-credit and fee-engine marks are the pressure point when IG is -4.9% over three months and LQD is at the 3.6th percentile.

ideas.name: Energy equities (XLE/XOP)
ideas.line: Long XLE and XOP: crude at 92.89, energy led the tape
ideas.expr: Buy XLE core, XOP for beta, 2:1. Fund partially by shorting OIH, which is rolling over (-10.7% on the month, acc -1.28).
ideas.thesis: Crude is up 35.2% on the quarter and 61.8% YTD with Brent at 102.51, yet XLE is only -2.6% on the month and energy's 3-month relative strength is +15.2% and still trending up. The equities have not discounted the strip, and oil/gold at +8.4% on the month says real-asset demand is rotating out of the metals and into the barrel.

ideas.name: Grid equipment vs power producers
ideas.line: Long GEV+ETN vs short CEG+VST: sell the megawatt, buy the box
ideas.expr: Equal-weight long GEV and ETN, short CEG and VST, beta-matched. Overlay long GRID vs short NLR for the ETF version.
ideas.thesis: The electrification trade is bifurcating. Equipment makers monetise the capex backlog regardless of power prices; independent power producers are long duration and long power-price optimism, both of which are being repriced at 5.6% on the 30-year. Buy the order book, sell the asset.

ideas.name: Short developed ex-US vs long S&P
ideas.line: Short EFA vs long SPY: dollar squeeze is breaking DM ex-US
ideas.expr: Sell EFA against an equal-notional long in SPY (or short EWG/EWU/EWI basket vs SPY if you want the Europe-only cut).
ideas.thesis: A 100th-percentile dollar is a direct earnings and flow tax on unhedged DM ex-US equity. The US index has semis to offset it; Europe has nothing — XLF-equivalent banks and exporters are the whole index and both are hostage to EUR and global funding.

ideas.name: Short Mexico equity (EWW) / long USDMXN
ideas.line: Short EWW: peso at 3-sigma break, Mexico index rolling over
ideas.expr: Short EWW outright or buy 2-3 month EWW puts; FX version is long USD/MXN via CME MXN futures.
ideas.thesis: The peso was the last high-carry EM currency still holding; it has now broken with the most extreme momentum reading on the board. Local equity in dollar terms takes both the FX hit and the risk-premium hit, and the local index is already rolling over in pesos.

ideas.name: Long semis vs short financials
ideas.line: Long SMH vs short XLF: the only trend that still pays
ideas.expr: Long SMH (or SOXX) against an equal-notional short in XLF; add BX or GS to the short leg for higher beta to the capital-markets unwind.
ideas.thesis: Financials are failing to monetise the steepest curve in a year, which means the market is pricing credit and capital-markets revenue risk, not NIM. Semis are the one group with accelerating relative strength and an actual order cycle. Own the momentum, fund it with the broken cyclical.

ideas.name: Long loans vs short high yield
ideas.line: Long BKLN vs short HYG: own the carry, not the duration
ideas.expr: Long BKLN against an equal-notional short HYG; size 1:1 since HYG carries roughly 3-4 years more duration.
ideas.thesis: This is the cleanest way to be short the credit crack without being short carry. Loans float off a 4.20% front end that isn't moving; HY bonds eat the entire 54bp monthly move in the 10y plus widening spreads. If credit is genuinely rolling over, HYG underperforms twice.

ideas.name: Long semis / short small caps
ideas.line: Long SMH vs short IWM, dollar-neutral — the only real leadership
ideas.expr: Long SMH, short IWM, equal notional. Rebalance weekly; express the long leg with SMH rather than single names to avoid AMD's 64% 200-day extension.
ideas.thesis: In a rising-real-rate tape, cash-generative AI capex compounders outperform the levered small-cap complex. The pair isolates leadership from index beta and from the duration risk that is hitting everything else.

ideas.name: Long Japan equities
ideas.line: Long EWJ / N225 futures; +3.7% with no yen devaluation
ideas.expr: Long EWJ, or Nikkei futures with a partial yen hedge. Do not use DXJ here — the point is the rally is not yen-driven.
ideas.thesis: Japan is the one developed market where the equity bid is domestic and the currency is behaving. With USDJPY flat and -1.7% on the month, a 3.7% index day is real risk appetite, not an FX translation effect, and relative strength vs the S&P has turned up.

ideas.name: Long Brazil vs EM
ideas.line: Long EWZ vs short EEM — the only EM with positive momentum
ideas.expr: Long EWZ, short EEM, equal notional. Take the pair off on any USDBRL break above 5.45.
ideas.thesis: Brazil is the one EM that is rallying through the dollar squeeze, with local equity momentum and a currency that is not participating in the LatAm carry unwind hitting Mexico.

ideas.name: Short financials / capital markets
ideas.line: Short XLF: curve steepened, banks fell anyway
ideas.expr: Short XLF outright, or buy Nov 52 puts; purer version is a short basket of BX/GS/IAI against a long SPY hedge.
ideas.thesis: If a 3m10y curve at the 100th percentile cannot lift bank stocks, the problem is asset marks, not net interest margin. Private-credit and capital-markets exposure is repricing in equity before it shows in spreads — and HYG/IEF at the 97.6th percentile means the credit market hasn't started.

ideas.name: Long XOP vs short OIH
ideas.line: Long XOP / short OIH: crude up, service capex broken
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long XOP, short OIH.
ideas.thesis: Crude is trading its own supply story, not a demand collapse — copper is up and copper/gold is at the 96.5th percentile. E&Ps monetise the barrel directly; oil service is the levered capex bet and it is being liquidated even as the commodity rallies.

ideas.name: Long bitcoin via IBIT
ideas.line: Long IBIT: whole complex flipped to turning_up, still cheap
ideas.expr: Long IBIT, sized small (1-2% NAV), add on a hold above the 200-day.
ideas.thesis: Bitcoin is the one risk asset that has already had its bear market — down 26.1% over a year — and is now re-accelerating off a low base while everything else is extended. It is the cleanest expression of any front-end easing that the 3-month and 2-year are hinting at.

ideas.name: Short OIH / long XLE
ideas.line: Short OIH vs long XLE: Brent -8% hits services, not majors
ideas.expr: Short OIH against a long in XLE, dollar-neutral; substitute XOM/CVX for XLE if you want less refining beta.
ideas.thesis: An 8% one-day break in Brent kills the marginal capex dollar long before it dents integrated cash flow. Services carry the operating leverage; majors carry the dividend and the buyback. The spread has already started and has room.

ideas.name: Short HYG vs long IEF
ideas.line: Short HYG vs IEF: spread 94th pct while HYG acc is -1.39
ideas.expr: Short HYG, long IEF in equal dollars (or buy HYG Dec 76 puts outright for convexity).
ideas.thesis: Duration has fully repriced — LQD and IEF at the 0th percentile — but the credit risk premium has not: HYG/IEF still sits at the 94th percentile. If the real-yield shock keeps grinding on leveraged balance sheets, that ratio mean-reverts before defaults ever appear.

ideas.name: Long SMH vs short KRE
ideas.line: Long semis vs regional banks: capex bid vs a 4.92% 2-year
ideas.expr: Equal-dollar long SMH, short KRE. Roll monthly.
ideas.thesis: Two ways to own the same rates shock: the AI complex is funded by cash flow and keeps making relative highs; regional banks are funded by a 2-year at 4.92% with 2s10s flattened to 32bp. The tape is paying for the first and charging for the second every single day.

ideas.name: Short EUR/USD
ideas.line: Short EURUSD 1.1322: 0th percentile, acceleration -1.88
ideas.expr: Short EURUSD spot or 6E futures; or long UUP as a proxy. 1% risk to the 1.1450 stop.
ideas.thesis: The dollar is being pulled higher by a 2.90% US real yield, and the euro is the funding casualty. Local European equity is fine — the currency is doing all the damage, which is exactly how these trends extend rather than exhaust.

ideas.name: Short oil services
ideas.line: Short OIH: Brent -7.7%, RBOB -9.6% on the month
ideas.expr: Short OIH; or pair long XLE / short OIH to isolate capex from reserves.
ideas.thesis: Services need a high and rising strip to justify a capex cycle. Crude just broke while the product crack has been collapsing for a month, and OIH has already lost its relative-strength trend — the equity is de-rating ahead of the commodity.

ideas.name: Short the front end (2-year)
ideas.line: Short ZT / 2y notes: bear flattener says hike, not supply
ideas.expr: Short Dec 2-year note futures (ZT), or buy Dec/Mar SOFR put spreads; cash proxy is short SHY against a flat 10y position (short ZT vs long TY at 2:1 duration to isolate the flattener).
ideas.thesis: The marginal seller has moved from the 30-year to the 2-year. With the 3-month bill up 38bp on the month and the 2-year up 58bp to 4.92%, the market is repricing the policy path, not just term premium. That has further to run than the long end, which is already 100th percentile and crowded short.

ideas.name: Long loans / short high yield & IG
ideas.line: Long BKLN, short HYG+LQD: own spread, not duration
ideas.expr: Long BKLN, short a duration-matched basket of HYG and LQD (roughly 60/40 by notional, ~1.2x BKLN notional to equalize vol).
ideas.thesis: Every dollar of pain in credit this month is discount rate, not default risk. Floating-rate loans capture the front-end repricing that is killing the fixed-rate index; HYG/IEF at the 96th percentile tells you spreads are fine, so short the duration and own the coupon reset.

ideas.name: Long gold vs short silver
ideas.line: Long GLD / short SLV: ratio 68 heading to 74 in a liquidation
ideas.expr: Long GLD, short silver futures or SLV at 1:1 dollar notional; scale to 1.3x short silver if using vol-weighting.
ideas.thesis: When the precious complex is being liquidated for margin rather than sold on fundamentals, the high-beta leg loses twice. Silver is already 16.3% below its 200-day versus gold's 8.8%, and the ratio has turned up. This monetizes day three of the unwind without betting on a bottom in bullion.

ideas.name: Long energy majors vs short transports
ideas.line: Long XOM+CVX / short IYT: $93 crude, freight rolling over
ideas.expr: Long an equal-weight XOM/CVX basket (or XLE), short IYT at equal dollar notional.
ideas.thesis: Crude at 93.55 is a cost for the freight complex and a cash flow for the majors. Energy relative strength is +12.6% over three months and turning up; transports are the single weakest relative line in the entire digest. This pays whether the tape is risk-on or risk-off, because it is an input-cost spread, not a beta bet.

ideas.name: Short the leverage complex vs healthcare
ideas.line: Short XLF & BX / long XLV: leverage derates, care re-rates
ideas.expr: Short XLF plus a satellite short in BX, long XLV at equal notional (2/3 XLF, 1/3 BX versus 1x XLV).
ideas.thesis: Rising front-end rates with flattening curve and 100+ MOVE compress exactly the businesses that live on leverage, deal flow and mark-to-market carry. Healthcare is the only defensive whose relative strength is turning up now that utilities and staples have broken. This is the cleanest way to short the derate without shorting the index at the 92nd percentile.

ideas.name: Short the US consumer at a 7% mortgage
ideas.line: Short XLY: mortgage 7.03%, HD and MCD at 52-week lows
ideas.expr: Short XLY outright or buy Dec 105 puts; size a portion in HD and MCD single-name puts. Cleaner as XLY vs XLP pair if you want beta out.
ideas.thesis: The rate shock transmits to the household through mortgages and revolving credit, and the tape already knows it: XLY -6.5% on the month in a down trend with acceleration -1.23, XLY/XLP -3.5% at the 13th percentile, HD -11.2% and MCD -11.0% both at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, UBER -13.2%, NKE at the 3rd percentile. Falling gasoline is the bull case and it hasn't helped for five weeks.

ideas.name: Floating rate over long-duration IG
ideas.line: Long BKLN vs short LQD: floating over long-duration IG
ideas.expr: Long BKLN, short LQD dollar-for-dollar (or short LQD vs long 2y Treasury futures if you want spread-only).
ideas.thesis: IG index duration is the purest loser of a term-premium repricing with no growth offset. LQD is -3.3% on the month at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks while loans are +0.4% on the month and +2.6% over 3 months at the 92nd percentile, because coupons reset with a 4.24% bill and defaults aren't the story yet.

ideas.name: Copper over gold, expressed in the miners
ideas.line: Copper over gold: long FCX vs short NEM, CU/AU 99th pctile
ideas.expr: Long FCX, short NEM, beta-balanced roughly 1:1 notional; add short GDX vs long COPX as the ETF version.
ideas.thesis: The same real-yield impulse that is killing bullion supports the industrial metal, because growth is not the problem: copper/gold is at the 99th percentile, +9.9% on the month with acceleration 1.69, while gold is 8.6% below its 200-day. Gold's monetary bid unwinds at 2.83% real yields; copper's physical bid doesn't.

ideas.name: Short the leverage complex, not the banks' credit
ideas.line: Short XLF: leverage complex derating, BX -19% on the month
ideas.expr: Buy XLF Dec 52 puts or short XLF; concentrate single-name shorts in BX and GS, avoid shorting KRE outright (deposit beta is already priced).
ideas.thesis: Financials were supposed to be the bear-steepener winner; they are the loser because marks, not margins, drive this cycle. XLF is -6.2% on the month (z=-1.48) with relative strength rolling over, while alternative managers and brokers — the entities carrying the duration and private marks — lead lower: BX -19.3% on the month (z=-1.99, acc -1.86), GS -10.8%, IAI -8.1%, KIE -6.6%.

ideas.name: Semis dispersion: quality compute vs the extended tail
ideas.line: Long NVDA+TSM vs short AMD, 64% above its 200-day
ideas.expr: Long a 50/50 NVDA-TSM basket, short AMD, equal notional; or sell AMD Nov upside calls against long SMH.
ideas.thesis: Semi leadership is intact but the beta has run too far ahead of the cash flows. AMD is +182.6% YTD and 64.1% above its 200-day with z=1.46; NVDA is 15.1% above its 200-day and made up ground today. When rates compress multiples, the highest-duration equity in the group gives back the most while the earners hold.

ideas.name: 2s30s bear steepener
ideas.line: Steepener: long 2y futures vs short ultra-bond
ideas.expr: Long TU (2y) futures vs short WN (ultra-bond) DV01-neutral, or buy a 2s30s steepener via swaps; retail proxy long SHY vs short TLT.
ideas.thesis: The rates shock is bifurcating. The Fed path can finally soften as oil collapses, but term premium and supply own the long end. 2s10s at 36bp is in the 30th percentile of the last year with the 30-year at the 100th — that is not a stable combination.

ideas.name: Transports vs S&P on the fuel crash
ideas.line: Long IYT vs short SPY: fuel down 9%, ratio at 52wk low
ideas.expr: Long IYT (or XTN for equal-weight), short an equivalent notional of SPY. 1:1 dollar-neutral.
ideas.thesis: Transports discount recession while their single biggest variable cost just collapsed. IYT/SPY is at the absolute 52-week low with a z-score of -2.63 — a two-sigma-plus dislocation into a 9.4% weekly drop in gasoline and a 6.2% fall in Brent.

ideas.name: Gold miners capitulation reversal
ideas.line: Long GDXJ: acceleration z=-2.75 with metal turning up
ideas.expr: Long GDXJ outright, or long GDX Dec call spreads. Add on a gold close back above its 200-day (currently 5.2% above spot).
ideas.thesis: The metals drawdown was statistical, not fundamental: gold -7.2% in a month with acceleration z=-3.2, GDX -3.12, NEM -3.2. Those are washout readings, and the miners' 3-month relative strength versus the S&P is still +13.7%. A stabilizing 10-year real yield removes the proximate cause of the selling.

ideas.name: BX as the private-credit canary
ideas.line: Short BX: -17.3% in a month while the S&P sits at highs
ideas.expr: Short BX outright or buy Jan puts; hedge with a long in XLF if you want sector-neutral.
ideas.thesis: The alternative managers are where a 4.98% five-year and a 52-week-low IG bond market actually bite: marks, fundraising and realization fees all compress. BX is down 17.3% on the month (z=-1.81) with acceleration -1.61 while the index made highs — that divergence usually resolves in the stock's direction.

ideas.name: Long USD vs MXN
ideas.line: Long USDMXN: acc z=1.78 while EM equities ignore it
ideas.expr: Long USD/MXN spot or 3-month forwards; alternatively buy 3-month USDMXN calls struck near 18.25.
ideas.thesis: The peso is the carry trade most exposed to a re-firming dollar and a collapsing oil price. USDMXN is +4.3% in a month with acceleration z=1.78 while EEM rose 1.1% today — EM equity is not yet discounting what EM FX is saying, and that gap tends to close toward the currency.

ideas.name: Long QQQ / short IWM
ideas.line: Own the cash-rich, short the floating-rate: QQQ vs IWM
ideas.expr: Long QQQ, short IWM, dollar-neutral, beta-adjusted ~0.85x on the IWM leg. Or long QQQ Dec calls vs short IWM Dec calls.
ideas.thesis: At a 4.87% 2-year and 5.03% 5-year, small caps' floating-rate debt stack is being repriced in real time while megacap tech funds itself from cash flow. QQQ/SPY is +4.0% in a month at z=1.53 and still accelerating; IWM/SPY is -6.0% and rolling over.

ideas.name: Long gold miners (GDX) into capitulation
ideas.line: GDX -12.5%/1m on -3.7 sigma acceleration; gold turning up
ideas.expr: Long GDX, add GDXJ for beta. Or long GDX Jan 95 calls. Size 1-2%, scale in — this is a washout trade, not a trend trade.
ideas.thesis: The miners have overshot the metal by a factor of two. GDX -12.5% versus gold -6.6% over a month, with acceleration z=-3.71 for GDX, -3.57 for GLD and -3.66 for NEM. Readings below -3 sigma on the second derivative are exhaustion, not information. GDX/gold is still +15.1% over three months, so the underlying re-rating is intact.

ideas.name: Fade the oil-beta equities (XOP)
ideas.line: Crude -8% but XOP only -4% 1w; energy hasn't marked down
ideas.expr: Short XOP, or buy Dec XOP 175 puts. Keep XLE/XOM long if you own them — this is a short of the high-beta E&P sleeve, not the majors.
ideas.thesis: The geopolitical premium is leaving crude faster than it is leaving energy equities. XOP is +1.1% on the month and +19.4% over three months against Brent now down 7.8% in a day and 5.4% on the week. Oil/gold fell 3.4% today after a 20% one-month surge — the ratio that has driven the whole energy relative trade is rolling.

ideas.name: Long crypto beta (IBIT + MSTR)
ideas.line: BTC +7%, SOL +18%, MSTR +27% 1m — all flipped to up
ideas.expr: Long IBIT as the core (2% position), add MSTR as the high-beta kicker (0.5%). Or long COIN Jan calls.
ideas.thesis: Crypto is the one liquid risk asset that bottomed and turned while equity breadth collapsed. BTC +41.4% and ETH +72.9% over three months, SOL +68.4%, all now in 'turning_up' trend state, yet BTC is only in the 40th percentile of its 52-week range and MSTR in the 29th — the recovery has barely started from a -22% year.

ideas.name: Homebuilders
ideas.line: Short ITB: mortgages above 7% and rising
ideas.expr: Short ITB (or XHB). Hedge-fund version: short ITB / long SPY.
ideas.thesis: The cleanest way to monetize the rates move. Mortgages are above 7%, builders are already cutting prices, and the group is in a relative downtrend with no bottom yet.

ideas.name: Oil tax on the consumer
ideas.line: Long XLE / short XLY: $107 Brent taxes the shopper
ideas.expr: Long XLE / short XLY, equal dollars
ideas.thesis: Brent at $107 and accelerating takes money from households and hands it to producers. Energy is the only sector with rising relative strength, while discretionary is in a relative downtrend. The pair profits if oil stays high even when the market falls.

ideas.name: Long bonds
ideas.line: Short TLT: the Fed is hiking and the 2-year leads
ideas.expr: Short TLT, or pay 10y/30y swaps. Alternatively sell 2y futures to express the Fed.
ideas.thesis: Druckenmiller says policy is still too easy and the Fed is now hiking into a weak-auction, big-deficit backdrop. The 2-year has moved most, so the market is still catching up to the Fed.

ideas.name: Fade parabolic semis, own software
ideas.line: Long IGV / short SOXX: AI build-out is late stage
ideas.expr: Long IGV / short SOXX (or trim MU, AMD)
ideas.thesis: Druckenmiller has cut AI to 20% of its peak and calls the build-out late stage. MU is 64% and AMD 73% above their 200-day averages, and semis are up 88% this year. Software has already been de-rated and is now turning up in relative strength.

ideas.name: Cheap crash protection
ideas.line: Buy SPY puts: VIX 16 while bond vol spikes
ideas.expr: Buy 2–3 month SPY puts ~5% OTM, or a put spread; alternatively short IYT vs SPY
ideas.thesis: Bond volatility is spiking but equity volatility is not. The VIX at 16 prices none of the rates, oil or breadth stress. When transports and equal-weight break first, the index usually follows.

ideas.name: Copper miners on the dip
ideas.line: Buy COPX: the metal is at a record, the miners are not
ideas.expr: Buy COPX or FCX on weakness, scaling in
ideas.thesis: Copper just set a record, but the miners fell 10% with the market. Miners lagging the metal is a gap that usually closes. Electrification and a hot economy back the metal.
